task_prefix.collision_check: No collision with existing prefixes. Verified against id_registry.json TSK_ context_prefixes_in_use. Nearest existing prefix is TSK_BLTN_* (built-in) — semantically distinct (cabinets vs built-in shelving).
task_prefix.naming_rule: TSK_CABT_{ACTION} — action should be verb-based (SAND_DOORS, FINISH_FRAMES, PROTECT_FLOOR, REMOVE_HARDWARE, REINSTALL_DOORS)

expected_modules.notes: Protection setup for all 9 zones. Hardware/door/drawer removal and labeling.
Fill fasteners, caulk joints, sand surfaces, MDF edge seal, clean dust.
Conditional on substrate_state=SS_BARE. Shellac edge seal (MDF) + primer coat on all items.
Finish coat application on all items (frames, doors, drawers, interiors).
Sand coat, inspect, patch, clean between coats. Run multiple times per round config.
Final quality inspection per tier standard. Touch-up after door/drawer reinstallation.

Remove protection, reinstall hardware/doors/drawers, clean work area. NOTE: Reassembly tasks (reinstall hardware, doors, drawers) are in cleanup phase because they happen after the 5-7 day cure period — this is the final mobilization.

module_prefix.notes: Research proposed 12 modules including separate MOD_CABT_DISASSEMBLY, MOD_CABT_REASSEMBLY, MOD_CABT_CURE, etc. Consolidated to 7 canonical modules per established pattern. Disassembly tasks fold into MOD_CABT_SETUP. Reassembly tasks fold into MOD_CABT_CLEANUP. The SOP Librarian may split further if workflow clarity requires it, but the 7-module base structure matches all prior fine-finish specs (BLTN, ARCH, WDCL, WDWL, WNSC, etc.).

quality_tier.notes: QT2 excluded — cabinet work does not have an economy tier. QT3 standard residential. QT4 premium (waterborne alkyd recommended). QT5 showroom (premium product mandatory).

application_method.notes: Research uses 'spray' and 'brush'. 'brush' in this context means brush/roll using Roll and Tip per Fine Finish Doctrine. Spray is strongly preferred. spray_backroll, spray_rolloff, roll, brush_roll are NOT used in this spec.

sheen.notes: Single values only. QT3 max satin. QT4 max semi-gloss. QT5 any including gloss. Gloss requires spray method.

phase.notes: This spec uses setup/prep/prime/interstage/finish/cleanup. 'apply' excluded — spec uses prime and finish directly. 'protect' and 'protection' are NEVER valid phase values.

unit_of_measure.notes: EA for doors/drawers/hardware, SF for frames/interiors/protection, LF for caulk/backsplash, EA_ROOM for room-level tasks, FIXED for tool cleaning.

substrate_state.notes: Input: SS_BARE (requires full primer workflow) or SS_PRIMED_FACTORY (primer optional). Output varies by sheen selection.

product_role.notes: Filtered to roles used by this spec. Primer for substrate coating, finish for topcoats, sealer for MDF edge seal.

modifier_mechanism.notes: QT3=baseline, QT4/QT5=selective_multiplier on qt_scaled tasks, QT5+brush=additional_rounds (3rd finish coat). baseline_reduction not used (no QT2).

NOTE: cabinet surface IDs are in the Reference doc but NOT yet in id_registry entries_in_active_use — they must be registered.

bonding_primer.notes: Research proposes SYS_PRIMER_BONDING for QT4+ cabinet adhesion. No exact match in registry — SYS_PRIMER_BONDING does not exist. The existing substrate-driven primers (wood_acrylic, MDF latex/shellac) cover most cases. However, research identifies a genuine need for a bonding primer for smooth/hard substrates and questionable factory primer. Propose new SYS_PRIMER_BONDING_CABINET or use generic SYS_PRIMER_BONDING. Given the reuse-over-creation principle, propose generic SYS_PRIMER_BONDING that can be shared across specs.

material_system_prefix.notes: CRITICAL MAPPING: Research uses SYS_PRIMER_SHELLAC, SYS_PRIMER_ACRYLIC_LATEX, SYS_PRIMER_BONDING which are NOT registered IDs. Downstream agents MUST use the registered equivalents listed above. The Materials Manager should map: SYS_PRIMER_SHELLAC (research) -> SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC (edges) + SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_SHELLAC (knot spots). SYS_PRIMER_ACRYLIC_LATEX (research) -> SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_ACRYLIC (wood) + SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX (MDF faces). SYS_PRIMER_BONDING (research) -> SYS_PRIMER_BONDING (new, proposed).

adjacency_notes: SF_BUILTIN_NC_v1: Sibling spec. Shares MDF edge seal protocol, shellac primer, door removal workflow, cure time. Scope boundary: cabinets with doors/drawers -> SF_CABINET_NC_PAINT. Open shelving/built-ins -> SF_BUILTIN_NC.
SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT_v1: Crown molding integral to cabinet tops -> SF_CABINET_NC_PAINT scope. Room crown meeting cabinet -> SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT scope.
SF_DOOR_SLAB_INT_NC_v1: Shares horizontal door painting methodology. Scope boundary: interior passage doors -> SF_DOOR_SLAB_INT_NC. Cabinet doors -> SF_CABINET_NC_PAINT.
SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC: Scheduling note — paint cabinets before walls when possible (overspray on unpainted drywall is easily covered).
SF_DRYWALL_CEILING_NC: Same scheduling note — cabinets before ceiling when possible.

RULE 5: Every PS_ key in production.json MUST match spec.json required_paintscope_inputs
RULE 6: Every zone_id in spec.json MUST match sop_modules.json protection_metadata.zones
RULE 7: Module phase order: setup -> prep -> prime -> interstage -> finish -> cleanup
RULE 8: UOM for a task MUST match between sop_modules.json and production.json
RULE 9: All TSK_CABT_ IDs must use the TSK_CABT_ prefix established in this resolution
